newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana Stenpad gold samples head for more tests.
newsitem.headline: Ghana Stenpad gold samples head for more tests.

text.p: Samples from the gold find of Canadian mining group Golden Rule/Hixon at Stenpad, Ghana, were flown abroad on Sunday for more tests after a Ghana Mines Commission check dismissed earlier estimates, the company's manager told Reuters on Monday.

"Associated (Mining Consultants) brought in an engineer and six security people who observed the drilling, taking of the samples. At no time have we had access to the sample they took," said acting managing director Cameron Stephen.

Associated Mining Consultants (AMC) was appointed by joint venture partners Golden Rule Resources and Hixon Gold Resources after earlier rumours that sample results were overstated prompted check assays by Ghana's Mines Commission.
Golden Rule/Hixon said in January gold assay results from a 100m trench at Stenpad, 65 km west of Obuasi, southwest Ghana, showed an average of 8.75 grammes of gold per tonne.

Check assays subsequently taken by the Mines Commission and Vancouver-based CME Consulting Ltd sent to Golden Rule's Calgary headquarters in May suggested the results were overstated. The share prices of Toronto-quoted Golden Rule and Vancouver-quoted Hixon headed down on the news.

About 28 boxes of samples from Stenpad were flown on Sunday night to an undislcosed destination in North America but assay results would not be made known until next week at the earliest, Stephen said, adding that Ghanaian public holidays had delayed the shipment.

Golden Rule/Hixon has also started an internal investigation of the assay results, said Stephen, a mining expert with 40 years of mining experience in Canada who has temporarily replaced managing director Glen Harper.
"I am doing my own investigation into the whole background of this problem," he told Reuters, adding that diamond drilling at Stenpad was unaffected.
Rumours that Stenpad assays had been "salted" -- or faked to give better gold deposit indications -- arose after Stenpad samples showed higher gold contents than in nearby areas.
Harper said on Friday that divergent test results could have resulted from the coarse nature of gold deposits in the Stenpad area.
"I'm eating my own cooking. I have faith in the project," he said, adding that he owned almost two million shares in Golden Rule.
AMC's report was due in mid-June, he said.

Shares in another Calgary-based miner Bre-X, an upstart exploration firm, dived from dizzy heights earlier this year on news that gold assays from its Busang site had overstated potential gold deposits.
